title: Enough is Enough march demanding accountability and better governance
location: Monrovia, from Congo Town toward the Executive Mansion / Capitol
scope: One reported city march; no additional location is combined.
organizer: STAND chair Mulbah K. Morlu and former representative Acarous Gray reported as leaders

state_target.evidence: Organizers intended to deliver a petition to the President and raised accountability, corruption, unemployment and poor services.

demands_original: Accountability, good governance, public services and economic hardship; exact petition text not available.
participants_original: Hundreds, as reported by one outlet; no counting methodology.
threshold_50_evidence: Source reports hundreds; threshold ≥50 is plausible and retained for review, but not independently corroborated.

start_date.summary: Articles report July 17 and July 10 respectively.

end_date.summary: No duration/end dates supplied; each is recorded as a dated gathering.

location.summary: Smart News gives route from Congo Town toward Executive Mansion; FPA says Monrovia and petition to Legislature.

scope.summary: Two distinct reported gathering dates/issues; transport action may connect to August LTM protests, not merged without review.

organizer.summary: STAND chair and former representative identified as leading July 17 march.

state_target.summary: Organizers intended to petition President over governance/accountability and public service concerns.

demands.summary: Demand grouped under political process/accountability category.

participants_original.summary: Source says hundreds; no count method.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative hundreds description supports threshold, single source and pending independent review.

state_response.summary: Police monitoring/barricades for march; separate transport protest source reports dispersal, linked to event E002.

notes: Single source and qualitative headcount; candidate is not officially reviewed or approved.
open_questions: Was the petition delivered and what were its exact demands?
Can an independent local report corroborate turnout and organizer account?
Did the July march lead to a continuous multi-day episode or was it a one-day event?

title: Ministry of Transport employees petition lawmakers over LTM concession
location: Monrovia, Legislature/Capitol route not further specified
scope: One ministry-employee assembly reported; relationship with August protest and other July LTM reports remains uncertain.
organizer: Ministry of Transport employees; exact lead organization unknown

state_target.target: Legislature and national transport policy/contract decision
state_target.evidence: A ministry employee says they were going to petition lawmakers against outsourcing driver licensing and vehicle plates to LTM, citing job risk and transparency.

demands_original: Oppose outsourcing contract functions and protect ministry functions/jobs; no exact written petition text saved.
participants_original: Over 200 employees, attributed to one employee.
threshold_50_evidence: Reported estimate over 200; no independent count or method, keep under review.

location.summary: Report places the protest in Monrovia on the way to petition lawmakers.

scope.summary: Ministry workers gathered around one contract petition; possible same LTM campaign reported in August.

organizer.summary: Ministry employees are described; exact organizing committee unknown.

state_target.summary: Workers planned to petition Legislature over a reported outsourcing deal.

demands.summary: Workers feared job losses from state-concession outsourcing; coded as labor/wage dispute.

participants_original.summary: Named ministry employee says she and over 200 employees gathered.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Attributed estimate exceeds 200, but no independent count method.

protester_violence.summary: Source describes gathering as peaceful before police intervention.

state_response.summary: Employee account alleges tear gas and dispersal by police.

notes: Possible continuing campaign into August; count once as an episode pending review.
open_questions: Was the July 10 gathering the same ongoing LTM protest described in July 22/August 4 reports?
Is there independent corroboration of the employee-attributed crowd estimate?
What was the formal contract status and petition target?
